WASAPI grr-noise root cause confirmed and reverted: AUTOCONVERTPCM was causing periodic 160-sample DC bias runs (~every 50ms, flags=0x0 — undetectable at WASAPI level). Root cause: Windows internal SRC delivers a slowly-drifting ramp during certain periods; our DC blocker converts this ramp to constant int16 output (apparent DC). OBS research confirmed: OBS never uses AUTOCONVERTPCM for capture. Fix applied to loopback_capture.cpp: (1) AUTOCONVERTPCM and SRC_DEFAULT_QUALITY flags REMOVED from all paths, (2) Initialize() now uses m_mixFormat (native device format, e.g. 48kHz stereo float32), (3) software box-average resampler (3-tap FIR, zeros at 16kHz/32kHz) RESTORED with m_resampleCursor state, (4) full format detection RESTORED in DecodePacketToMonoFloat (EXTENSIBLE/IEEE_FLOAT/PCM + channel averaging), (5) kMicGainFactor=8.0 added after resampling before DC blocker to compensate low mic level. [Debug] log line removed.

CRACKLING ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED AND FIXED. Root cause: NativeCallable.listener is fully async — it posts the pointer VALUE to Dart's event loop and returns immediately. The local std::vector<int16_t> pcmData was destroyed before Dart read from the pointer, causing use-after-free. On Windows heap, the next loop iteration's pcmData allocation reused the same address, corrupting the data Dart was reading. This bug was present across every version and masked by louder symptoms (AUTOCONVERTPCM DC bias, DC blocker artifacts, heartbeat zero injection). Fix: C++ now heap-allocates with new uint8_t[] before calling callback; Dart calls Audio_FreeBuffer (new FFI export) immediately after Uint8List.fromList copy. Result confirmed: crackling gone, outPeak 2245-5797 (clean, no 32767 clipping), needsMicGain=0 for loopback. Remaining: low loopback level (~-15dBFS) is Windows Stereo Mix volume, not a code issue — IndicConformer per-feature normalization handles it.

OBS WASAPI reference implementation analyzed (github.com/obsproject/obs-studio/plugins/win-wasapi/win-wasapi.cpp). Key findings: (1) AUDCLNT_STREAMFLAGS_EVENTCALLBACK always set — pure event-driven, no Sleep() polling, (2) 5-second buffer (BUFFER_TIME_100NS=50000000) to prevent overflow between reads, (3) SetEventHandle() called after Initialize(), (4) CaptureThread uses WaitForSingleObject(event, 10ms) — 10ms timeout fallback for loopback silence periods, (5) no SetClientProperties, (6) native GetMixFormat() format passed directly. Applied to loopback_capture.cpp: AUDCLNT_STREAMFLAGS_EVENTCALLBACK added, m_captureEvent HANDLE added, Initialize buffer=5s, SetEventHandle called, CaptureThread Sleep(10) replaced with WaitForSingleObject(m_captureEvent, 10), heartbeat injection on WAIT_TIMEOUT preserved, CloseHandle in Stop(). Platform: Windows-only. Pending: rebuild and WAV validation.

Applied four-part Intel SST WASAPI fix to loopback_capture.cpp: (1) buffer duration 1s->20ms to prevent DSP sleep, (2) 200ms Sleep() + stat reset after Start() for DSP wake, (3) stats window extended to 20 packets to capture warm-up curve, (4) near-zero warning added. IAudioClient2::SetClientProperties(AudioCategory_Communications) added for beamforming/AGC activation — confirmed hr=0x0.

Stereo Mix selected as microphone when user clicked Start In-Person Meeting. Root cause: GetDefaultAudioEndpoint(eCapture, eConsole) returned Stereo Mix because user had enabled it as the Windows default input device for the Live Meeting loopback path. The needsMicGain flag was also incorrectly set to true for Stereo Mix (Stereo Mix is already line-level, 8x gain causes clipping). Fix: replaced default-endpoint fallback for mic path with two-stage FormFactor-based detection — Stage 1: PKEY_AudioEndpoint_FormFactor == Microphone(4)/Headset(5)/Handset(6) + virtual-device name guard; Stage 2: LineLevel(2) + name guard (catches USB mics, Focusrite, Blue Yeti); Fallback: GetDefaultAudioEndpoint only if both stages fail. selectedRealHardwareMic=true only on stages 1 and 2, driving m_needsMicGain.

Live Meeting loopback path changed from Stereo Mix preference to OBS-style pure render loopback. Old approach: enumerate eCapture endpoints, prefer device whose name contains 'stereo mix' (fragile, Realtek-only, locale-dependent). New approach: GetDefaultAudioEndpoint(eRender, eMultimedia) + AUDCLNT_STREAMFLAGS_LOOPBACK. This is 100% universal (Windows Vista+, every OEM, every audio chip), Stereo Mix setup is no longer required, and the approach matches how OBS, TeamViewer, and Sound Recorder capture system audio.

UI renamed Start Capture -> two separate actions: 'Start In-Person Meeting' (useMic=true, mic capture) and 'Start Live Meeting' (useMic=false, system audio loopback). Diagnosed and fixed resampler aliasing noise. Root cause: for 48k->16k (step=3.0), linear interpolation fraction is always 0.0 — pure decimation with no anti-aliasing filter. Every 8-24 kHz band aliases into voice band producing grr/grinding noise. Fix: replaced linear interpolation with box-average filter (ceil(step)=3 taps), placing filter zeros at exactly 16kHz and 32kHz. WAV spectral analysis confirmed HP/LP ratio dropped to 0.06x (noise eliminated).

Bluetooth SCO (HP OmniBook driver) confirmed as a separate noise source — not a code problem. Fix: disable Hands-Free Telephony toggle in Windows BT settings. This is independent of the Intel SST amplitude/aliasing issues.

VadUtteranceSegmenter flushing-state fix: silence frames were not being accumulated in the utterance buffer during flushing state, causing trailing phonemes to be cut off before ASR received them. One-line fix: added _utteranceBuffer.addAll(frame) inside the flushing/silence branch before the silence counter check. All three pre-written contract tests pass analytically.

DC blocker and kMicGainFactor decisions: (1) Added first-order IIR DC blocker (alpha=0.9999) targeting Intel SST -10.7% DC bias — then removed; Windows audio processing (AGC, AudioCategory_Communications pipeline) handles DC and gain normalization. (2) Added kMicGainFactor=8.0 for manual amplification — then removed; caused 18% sample clipping. Windows AGC with AUTOCONVERTPCM flags is the correct gain path.

This lets Windows handle format conversion and sample-rate quality internally rather than requiring the app to match the mix format exactly. Loopback path unchanged (AUDCLNT_STREAMFLAGS_LOOPBACK).

biography_of_the_12_hour_build.the_saga: A marathon debugging session focused on stabilizing the Windows loopback capture and AI intelligence pipeline. The build evolved from a mock-heavy simulation to a production-grade infrastructure with real-time hardware probing and diarization.
biography_of_the_12_hour_build.the_wasapi_starvation: DISCOVERY: WASAPI Loopback yields zero packets when system audio is silent. PREVIOUS ERROR: Injected arbitrary int16 zeros in C++, which clobbered the byte alignment for the downstream Float32 ONNX tensors.
biography_of_the_12_hour_build.the_lid_vad_misclassification: DISCOVERY: Models reported AKA/RON/HUN (garbage) because they were fed unaligned 'digital static' from improper Int16->Float32 normalization. RESOLUTION: Standardized on ByteData-backed direct normalization in the native layer to preserve 1:1 audio fidelity.
biography_of_the_12_hour_build.the_isolate_death: DISCOVERY: The background isolate would silently terminate due to a rank mismatch in the SpeakerEmbedder model (Expected rank 3, received rank 2). Bypassed Dart catch blocks. RESOLUTION: Formalized rank [1, 1, samples] for all speaker embeddings.
biography_of_the_12_hour_build.the_hardware_pivot: PIVOT: Shifted from generic DirectML to Intel oneAPI SYCL and OpenVINO to target modern, high-end PC performance as per the updated project scope.

decisions_taken: Adopt Platform-Agnostic Ingestion Contract: Native layers MUST handle resampling and normalization.
Implement Native Heartbeat: Inject zero-padded Float32 in C++ to keep Dart isolates active.
Use Intel oneAPI SYCL as primary Windows accelerator; fallback to DirectML.
Implement 15s Auto-Flush in Background Engine to prevent SBD infinite buffering.
Use 2-second Rolling Sliding Window for LID to support code-switching (multilingual speech).
For Indic cloud lane, send only VAD/LID decision + canonical header metadata + PCM/WAV chunk payload; avoid raw model internals in normal mode.
Remove LID from MVP hot path; treat language detection as diagnostic/advisory until multilingual ASR is proven.
Adopt uncertainty-aware speaker attribution: low-confidence, noisy, overlapping, or too-short segments must be marked Uncertain Speaker and reviewed before compliance-grade export.

Hindi/English MVP must prove consent-aware transcript flow: late speakers continue through engine as pending, non-consented content is redacted/excluded by default, and IndicTrans2-style translation is used only for host review/export of consented content.
All models must be configurable by registry/profile; Sherpa speech tasks, IndicTrans2 translation, and future IndicConformer candidates must be swappable independently.
Use quarantine-first storage for pending speakers: pending segments are retained locally but export-ineligible; later consent can release them only under audited retroactive consent policy.
Python model examples are reference paths only; production conversion requires documented preprocessing/tokenizer/tensor/decoding contracts and parity tests before C++/DLL or Dart integration.

Future optimization split: Sherpa-ONNX is the audio runtime path; IndicTrans2 is a separate text-to-text translation lane via ONNX Runtime/CTranslate2; IndicConformer 600M conversion belongs to VVC Docker/NeMo experiments after Flutter MVP proof.
For Sherpa/ASR/speaker models, the canonical model boundary remains 16kHz mono Float32; WASAPI loopback resampling must happen natively, not via naive Dart downsampling.

Task 1 segmentation is locked as an edge-triggered utterance segmenter because VAD truth alone was insufficient for offline ASR quality: use 300ms rolling pre-roll to recover clipped starts, 400ms silence tolerance to avoid premature flush, 1200ms minimum utterance to reject garbage-short decodes, and 250ms tail overlap to reduce boundary word loss.

Android Exynos 1280/M33 is a deferred CPU-only target: no NPU/GPU ONNX path is assumed, MediaProjection is the Android loopback analogue, and model memory sequencing must load ASR/TTS on demand rather than keeping the full stack resident.

If current Windows mic capture remains unresolved on Intel SST, the continuation strategy is not another ASR/VAD tweak; it is a product-grade Audio Device Intelligence Layer: detect device family/profile, apply profile-specific WASAPI settings and wake delays, validate early packet health, auto-recover dead streams, and surface device health/profile back to Flutter UI.

DECISION (2026-05-27): NativeCallable.listener is fully async — the pointer value is posted to Dart's event loop and the C++ stack frame is destroyed before Dart reads from it. Rule: never pass a pointer to stack-allocated or std::vector-local memory across NativeCallable.listener. Always heap-allocate with new uint8_t[], call the callback with the heap pointer, and export Audio_FreeBuffer so Dart can free after Uint8List.fromList copy.

DECISION (2026-05-27): Live Meeting uses OBS-style render loopback exclusively — GetDefaultAudioEndpoint(eRender, eMultimedia) + AUDCLNT_STREAMFLAGS_LOOPBACK. Stereo Mix is not required and should not be set as the Windows default input device. This approach works on every Windows installation regardless of OEM, audio chip, or driver. Stereo Mix setup instructions removed from INSTALLATION.md.

DECISION (2026-05-27): In-Person Meeting mic selection uses PKEY_AudioEndpoint_FormFactor (locale-independent, WHQL-certified) as the primary signal. Stage 1 = FormFactor 4/5/6 (Microphone/Headset/Handset — real hardware mics), Stage 2 = FormFactor 2 (LineLevel — USB mics, audio interfaces, Focusrite, Blue Yeti), virtual-device name guard on both stages, Fallback = GetDefaultAudioEndpoint only if both stages fail. m_needsMicGain is true only for stages 1 and 2 (real hardware), not for fallback or Stereo Mix.

DECISION (2026-05-27): Session WAV is always saved automatically using a streaming writer — 44-byte placeholder header at start, PCM chunks streamed to disk per bytesStream event, real header written on stop. BytesBuilder full-session accumulation removed. Minimum threshold _minimumSessionWavBytes enforced before header finalization. File path surfaced to UI via SESSION_WAV_SAVED IPC. User exports to Documents via drawer action.

DECISION (2026-05-27): Device picker is the user-facing recovery path for 'audio bar not moving'. No technical jargon exposed — just a list of device names with 'Auto-detect (default)' option. Preference persisted in SharedPreferences (preferred_mic_device / preferred_loopback_device). Meeting restarts automatically on device change if a meeting is active.

DECISION (2026-05-27): modelingUnit: 'bpe' is a required field for all IndicConformer-based ASR configs.
